name: Alruba
description: A star 165 parsecs away, 4.6 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 86782: radius 4.623 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 113.429 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.152) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 86782: effective temperature 8767 +/- 546 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.025)

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 86782: distance 165.285 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.096), at which the luminosity and radius hold

limb.none: no mass is measured and no spectroscopic surface gravity is published with this radius: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770 assume the gravity of their fit (table column 15)

text.card: A star 165 parsecs away, 4.6 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 113 times the Sun's luminosity at 8,767 K, so 4.623 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 86782: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q
